clue.text: A little balalaika to play on

indicators.note: a little of something is only a small part of it, so the letters sit inside the longer run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the instrument's name and the next two words

explanation.surface: A small Russian stringed instrument offered to someone to strum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little balalaika' reads as a toy instrument; it is the signal that the answer is a small part of the words that follow, spanning BALALAIK(A TO P)LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are prepositions describing position resting upon the upper surface of something.

clue.text: Doppelganger quaffs Irish whiskey, say

indicators.note: to quaff is to drink, taking something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: an exact double is the spit, as in the spitting image
IR is the standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A lookalike knocks back a glass of Irish whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish whiskey' looks like a single drink, but the words split: Irish gives IR, and 'whiskey, say' is the definition. Someone's double is their 'spit', short for the spitting image.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskey is one example of distilled strong liquor, which is called a spirit; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Turn on waterworks when electrical device switched over

indicators.note: switching something over flips it end to end, so the word runs the opposite way

parts.note: a light bulb is a common electrical device

explanation.surface: Someone bursts into tears when a gadget is switched off or flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched' suggests turning an electrical device on or off, but here it means turned the other way round. To turn on the waterworks is a British idiom for starting to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Blub is informal British slang for weeping noisily, which is what turning on the waterworks idiomatically describes.

clue.text: Lack of lids flipped up? Exactly!

indicators.note: in a down entry, flipping something upward makes it read from bottom to top, the other way round

parts.note: a lack of something is no such thing
lids are tops

explanation.surface: Someone notices the lids have been flipped up and so are missing, and agrees emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: NO TOPS read upwards gives SPOT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is a British informal phrase meaning precisely correct, used as an emphatic agreement just like the exclamation.

clue.text: Foody, our chap filling in empty grid

indicators.note: filling something goes inside it, so these pieces are placed within the other
an empty word has lost its contents, keeping only its outermost letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain
taken as written
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A food lover, our man, filling in a blank crossword grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grid' fits the crossword setting and 'empty' seems to describe a blank puzzle, which hides that only the word's outside letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a person devoted to eating and drinking, which is what a foodie, here spelt foody, is.

clue.text: Two fishes, one of those in quartet?

parts.note: two of something is a double
bass are fish, and the plural is the same as the singular

explanation.surface: Pairs of fish, and a question about a musical quartet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two fishes' suggests the zodiac sign Pisces, but it splits into two pieces. The question mark admits that a jazz quartet, rather than a string quartet, is the likely home of this instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest bowed string instrument often plays the bottom line in a jazz group of four musicians.

clue.text: The odd man out in Italy, cap askew

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the unusual one; the answer is the adjective describing him

indicators.note: something askew is out of its proper alignment, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In Italy, the one man who stands out wears his hat at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap askew' paints a jaunty hat, but askew is the anagram signal for ITALY plus CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the odd one out means not conforming to the usual pattern, so the person is unrepresentative or irregular.

clue.text: Framework has female relative supporting cousins, primarily

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever supports another piece sits beneath it, so it comes later
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written
SIS is short for sister

explanation.surface: A family structure where a sister supports the cousins.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer SIS 'supporting' the rest means it sits underneath, at the end. 'Has' is taken literally, not as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a car or other vehicle, the structural skeleton on which everything is mounted.

clue.text: Tiny particle for unit of weight

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A minute particle used as a measure of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word joining the definition, but it is PRO, meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a subatomic particle carrying positive charge, found in every atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Ancient city quarter within South Africa

indicators.note: something within another is enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a quarter is a part of something

explanation.surface: An old district of a city located in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City quarter' reads as a district, but the definition stops at 'city' and quarter is a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of classical Greece, famous for its military discipline.

clue.text: Wraparound garment other baby cut off

indicators.note: something cut off loses its end, so the final letter goes
letters wrapped around are twisted out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its final letter removed

explanation.surface: A wrap garment for the other baby has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraparound garment' looks like one phrase defining the answer, and a bathrobe is one, but wraparound is the signal to mix OTHER plus BAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose dressing gown worn before or after bathing, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Even on a Tuesday in February?

definitions.text: Even on a Tuesday in February?

parts.note: surface reading: something level, such as a surface
setter's reading: Shrove Tuesday, usually in February, is Pancake Day in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday, the day before Lent, is called Pancake Day in Britain because pancakes are eaten then; it often falls in February. 'Even' means perfectly level.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something completely level or smooth, and the pancake link ties it to that particular Tuesday.

clue.text: Wacky proposition for movement

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A crazy idea put forward in favour of a movement.
explanation.walkthrough: A motion is the formal term for a proposal debated at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the act or power of moving from place to place, a formal word for motion.

clue.text: Something with a stone on top of bolt, bolt upright

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a plum is a fruit with a stone

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A weight sits on top of a bolt that stands straight up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' appears twice: the first gives only its top letter, the second belongs to the definition. A stone is the hard seed in a fruit, not a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb means exactly vertical, as shown by a weighted plumb line, the same as standing perfectly straight.

clue.text: Tail docked on rear of rabbits

indicators.note: in an across entry, a piece placed on another comes after it
the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
docked means cut short

explanation.surface: A tail cut short on the hindquarters of rabbits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures docking a tail, but docked is simply CUT, placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer, a specialised word for that tail.

clue.text: Brown bilge turned solid

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: something turned has been twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dirty brown bilge water has gone solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests the bilge has gone off or set; it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangible means able to be touched, real and concrete, which matches the sense of solid as substantial.

clue.text: Pack things

definitions.meaning: second meaning: possessions or miscellaneous items

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to pack belongings, but the two words are separate meanings, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for cramming something full and a noun for unspecified belongings or material.

clue.text: A fish swimming, on form

indicators.note: something swimming moves about freely, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish swimming well, in good form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On form' reads as a phrase meaning performing well; it splits, with ON as letters and form as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to shape or make it, and to form is to give shape, so both verbs match.

clue.text: Grey swan drifts back

indicators.note: drifting back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: Shakespeare, the Bard, was called the Swan of Avon

explanation.surface: A grey swan floats backwards on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey swan' looks like a description of a bird; grey is the definition, and the Swan of Avon is Ben Jonson's name for Shakespeare, known as the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and lacking colour, which is the figurative sense of grey as dreary.

clue.text: Chicanery is king in financial operation

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so the piece is placed inside

parts.note: money as an adjective, as in money matters
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a business is an operation or enterprise

explanation.surface: Cheating is rife at the top of a financial firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Financial operation' reads as one phrase, which hides that the king goes inside only the first word's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for mischievous or dishonest behaviour, the same trickery as chicanery.

clue.text: Alien residing in semi, green!

indicators.note: something residing in a place lives inside it, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial lives in a semi-detached house and is green.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house, one of a joined pair. The answer runs through S(EMI GRE)EN.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre has left their native country to settle abroad, so in the new country they are a foreigner.

clue.text: Parking in lanes that's problematic in Italian city

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
something problematic is troubled and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking in narrow lanes is a headache in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside a rearrangement of LANES. The second 'in' simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a large port on the south-west coast of Italy, capital of the Campania region.

clue.text: Remarkable boxing

definitions.meaning: second meaning: hitting with the fists

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it praises a fighter; the two words are separate meanings, one an adjective and one a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means attracting attention by being impressive, and also hitting someone, as fighters do in a ring.

clue.text: Cut oxygen, say, and hydrogen

parts.note: oxygen is an example of a gas
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Reducing the supply of oxygen and hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a verb acting on the gases; it is the noun definition. 'Say' marks oxygen as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep wound or slash, a severe cut in skin or a surface.

clue.text: Reveal what the devil might create?

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a creation is a work of art

explanation.surface: Uncovering what the Devil might be capable of making.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a cryptic description: art made by an imp would be IMP ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to make it known or disclose it, the same as revealing it.

clue.text: Music from one of the Stones?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a genre of popular music
second meaning: a single stone, a boulder

explanation.surface: Music performed by a member of the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S points to the band, who do play this music; the question mark admits that a stone, lower case, is just a lump of mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a style of guitar-led popular music and also a large piece of mineral material.

clue.text: Mistake made, one yelping

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a creature that cries out loudly

explanation.surface: Someone makes an error and yelps about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A blunder so bad it makes people laugh is called by the same word as an animal that cries out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a glaring, embarrassing blunder and literally means a creature that lets out long cries.

clue.text: Time line?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prison term, as in doing time
second meaning: a line of text, a group of words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Time line' reads as a single word for a chronology; split, time is a term in prison and a line is written words, with the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge passes a prison term on a convict, and a grammatical unit of words is also called by this name.
